helpTooltips.saveError: Could not save the help setting. It only applies until the page is reloaded.

newWindow.what: Opens an empty form to schedule a new maintenance window on the currently selected status page.
newWindow.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Statushafen then sets the status itself from start and end: Scheduled, In Progress, Completed.
newWindow.example: Create a maintenance window for the database update on Saturday from 02:00 to 03:00.

search.what: Filters the list by title, message and affected components.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved. The search combines with the state filter next to it.
search.example: Type “API” to see all maintenance windows affecting the API.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (scheduled windows only; “View” without edit permission) and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: Running and completed windows can no longer be edited because their flow has already started. Deleting removes the window and its reminder from the status page and cannot be undone in the interface; the components' status is not reset.
rowActions.example: Delete a cancelled maintenance before it starts so it no longer shows under “Scheduled Maintenance”.

loadMore.what: Loads the next up to 200 maintenance windows. Only shown when there are more.
loadMore.effect: The new entries are appended to the list; search and filter then apply to them as well. Nothing is saved.
loadMore.example: A window from last year is not found: click “Load more” and search again.

template.what: Picks a maintenance template (from “Templates”) as a starting point. Only shown when creating and when templates exist.
template.effect: Title, message and affected components are taken from the template, with the language switch also the texts of the other languages. Start and end never come from the template. Everything stays editable afterwards.
template.example: Pick the template “DB maintenance”, set only the times and save.

title.what: The heading of the maintenance window. Required.
title.effect: Shown on the public status page under “Scheduled Maintenance”, from the start with the current incidents, and in the notifications.

message.what: The description for visitors, with formatting via the toolbar (bold, lists, links). Required; “Preview” shows the result.
message.effect: Appears on the public status page with the maintenance window and in the notifications to internal users and subscribers.
message.example: “The database is being updated. Short API interruptions are possible between 02:00 and 03:00.”

components.what: The components affected during the maintenance. Multiple choice, at least one.
components.effect: From the start they are set to “Maintenance”, from the end back to “Operational”, even if they had an outage before. Subscribers who subscribed to at least one of them are notified.
components.example: Pick “API” and “Web app” if both may be unavailable during the database update.

tags.what: Limits the scope of the maintenance window via tags, for example by region. Optional, only visible to global admins.
tags.effect: Visitors can filter by these tags on the status page, and internal emails only go to users with matching tags. Users who have tags themselves may only edit windows that share a tag with them.
tags.example: Set the tag “EU”: the maintenance shows up under the filter “EU”, and an editor with only “US” cannot change it.

start.what: Start of the planned work, in your local time. Required.
start.effect: At the start (checked every minute) the window switches to “In Progress”, the components go to “Maintenance” and a “Started” notification is sent. If the start is already in the past when you create it, the maintenance runs immediately.

end.what: Planned end of the work. Required; must be after the start.
end.effect: At the end the window switches to “Completed”, the components return to “Operational” and an “Ended” notification is sent. The time does not count as downtime in the 90-day availability.

reminder.what: Lead time for a reminder before the start: number and unit (minutes, hours, days). 0 means no reminder.
reminder.effect: Statushafen sends the reminder once, as soon as the start is closer than the lead time, to internal users and affected subscribers. If the lead time has already passed when you save, it goes out within a minute.
reminder.example: “1” and “Days”: subscribers are reminded one day before the database update.

save.effect: Creates the maintenance window or applies your changes. It takes effect on the status page immediately, internal users and affected subscribers are notified, and the entry is recorded in the audit log. Nothing is saved without title, message, component, start and end.
save.example: Move the end from 03:00 to 04:00 and save.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the maintenance window stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

newNotice.what: Opens an empty form for a new notice on the currently selected status page.
newNotice.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Notices are general messages without components and without a status history.

search.what: Filters the list by title and message.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved. The search combines with the active/inactive filter next to it.
search.example: Type “support” to find all notices about support hours.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (“View” without edit permission), “Translations” when there are several languages, and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: Deleting removes the notice from the status page immediately and cannot be undone in the interface; no emails are sent. To just hide it, untick “Active”.
rowActions.example: Delete an outdated notice about a feature that was introduced long ago.

title.what: The heading of the notice. Required.
title.effect: Shown on the public status page in the “Announcements” section and in the subject of emails to subscribers.

message.what: The text of the notice, with formatting via the toolbar (bold, lists, links). Required; “Preview” shows the result.
message.effect: Appears on the public status page below the title and, if enabled, in the emails to subscribers.
message.example: “From 1 Nov we are available around the clock.”

level.what: The level of the notice: Info, Warning or Critical.
level.effect: Determines color and icon on the public status page and the prefix in the default email subject ([INFO], [WARN], [CRITICAL]). Whether and when the notice appears does not depend on it.
level.example: New feature: “Info”. Shutdown of an old access next week: “Warning”.

active.what: Switches the notice on or off.
active.effect: Only active notices appear publicly, and only between start and end. If “Notify subscribers by email” is set, switching on triggers the “Created” email and switching off the “Ended” email.
active.example: Save a prepared notice as inactive first and activate it on the due date.

collapsed.what: Shows the notice collapsed to save space.
collapsed.effect: It is not shown directly on the status page but grouped behind “Show … more announcement(s)”.
collapsed.example: Collapse a permanent, less important note about privacy changes.

notifySubscribers.what: Sends emails about this notice to all active email subscribers of the status page.
notifySubscribers.effect: Emails go out on creation or activation (“Created”), when an active notice is edited (“Updated”) and on deactivation (“Ended”). Without the tick no email is sent; webhook subscribers never receive notices.
notifySubscribers.example: Switch it on for changed support hours, leave it off for a small note about the layout.

start.what: From when the notice is shown, in your local time. Optional.
start.effect: Before this time it is not publicly visible, even when active. Empty means: immediately.
start.example: 1 Nov, 00:00, so the note only appears from the due date.

end.what: Until when the notice is shown. Optional; must be after the start.
end.effect: Afterwards it disappears from the status page but stays in this list and still counts as active. Empty means: unlimited.
end.example: End of the promotion week, so the note does not have to be removed by hand.

save.effect: Creates the notice or applies your changes. It takes effect on the status page immediately and is recorded in the audit log; emails go out depending on “Notify subscribers by email”. Nothing is saved without title and message.
save.example: Change the level from “Info” to “Warning” and save.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the notice stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

search.what: Filters the “All status pages” table by the status page’s name or short name (slug), ignoring case.
search.effect: Applies as you type and only to this table: the figures at the top stay the totals across all status pages. Clicking a row opens that page’s incidents.
search.example: Type “acme” to see only the status page “Acme Corp” (/acme) and check its open incidents.

newIncident.what: Opens an empty form for a new incident on the currently selected status page.
newIncident.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Then the incident appears on the public status page right away, and internal users as well as subscribers of the affected components are notified.
newIncident.example: Sign-in is failing: create an incident “Login not possible” for the component “Web app”.

filter.what: Limits the list to all, only open or only resolved incidents.
filter.effect: Incidents in “Investigating”, “Identified” or “Monitoring” are open, those in “Resolved” are resolved. The filter only affects this list and can be combined with the search.
filter.example: Choose “Open” to see only the ongoing ones during several outages.

search.what: Searches the loaded incidents by title, message and the names of the affected components.
search.effect: Applies as you type, together with the status filter, and changes nothing about the incidents. Older incidents that are not loaded yet are only found after “Load more”.
search.example: Type “payment” to find all incidents of the payments API.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (“View” without edit permission), “Post update” (jumps to the update form in the detail view), “Translations” when there are several languages, and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: A deleted incident disappears from the public status page together with its history and post-mortem, and from the availability calculation; this cannot be undone in the interface. Subscribers are not notified when deleting, but they are for an update.
rowActions.example: Delete an incident that was accidentally created twice; set a real, finished incident to “Resolved” with an update instead.

loadMore.what: Loads the next 200 older incidents and appends them to the list.
loadMore.effect: The list first shows the 200 newest incidents; only after loading more do search and filter cover the older ones too. The button disappears once everything is loaded.
loadMore.example: Looking for an incident from last year: click “Load more” until it shows up in the list.

template.what: Picks an incident template whose title, message, status and affected components are copied into the form. Only shown when creating and when templates exist.
template.effect: The values are copied once when you choose the template and overwrite what you entered; afterwards they stay freely editable, and later changes to the template do not affect the incident. With several languages, the template’s translations are copied too.
template.example: Choose the template “Standard outage” and only add the affected service to the title.

title.what: The headline of the incident. Required.
title.effect: Shown on the public status page, in the list here and in the notifications to subscribers and internal users.
title.example: “Login not possible” or “API outage in region EU-West”.

message.what: The description of the incident for visitors, with simple formatting (bold, italic, lists, links). Required.
message.effect: Shown on the public status page as the initial report at the bottom of the history and included in the notifications. Later updates do not overwrite it.
message.example: “We are investigating errors when signing in. Users who are already signed in are not affected.”

status.what: The initial state of the incident: Investigating, Identified, Monitoring or Resolved. Only when creating; afterwards you change it with an update in the detail view.
status.effect: As long as the incident is not “Resolved”, it is open: it is listed under “Current incidents”, and its components show at least the status of its severity. “Resolved” lists it under “Past incidents” and records the end time.
status.example: Outage reported, cause unknown: “Investigating”. Adding an outage that is already fixed: “Resolved” with start and end.

severity.what: How badly the incident hits the components: Degraded Performance (default), Partial Outage or Major Outage. Can be changed later.
severity.effect: While the incident is open, the status page shows its components with at least this status. In the availability, its duration counts 30 %, 60 % or 100 % as downtime.
severity.example: Some payments fail: “Partial Outage”. Nothing works any more: “Major Outage”.

startedAt.what: When the incident actually began, in your local time. Optional.
startedAt.effect: Sets the start in the availability calculation and the order of incidents; without it, the time of creation counts. The end must not be earlier.
startedAt.example: The outage had been running since 09:40 and is reported at 10:15: set the start to 09:40.

resolvedAt.what: When the incident was resolved, in your local time. Only allowed with status “Resolved”.
resolvedAt.effect: Ends the incident in the availability calculation. If the field stays empty with “Resolved”, Statushafen records the time it was closed; an update to an open status clears the end again.
resolvedAt.example: Adding yesterday’s outage afterwards: status “Resolved”, start 14:00, end 14:45.

components.what: The components of this status page that are affected by the incident. Multiple choice, at least one.
components.effect: The status page shows the incident for these components and, while it is open, their status at least according to the severity. Subscribers who subscribed to at least one of them are notified.
components.example: Sign-in is broken: select “Web app” and “API”, but not “Email delivery”.

tags.what: Assigns tags to the incident, such as regions. Multiple choice; with nothing selected it has no tag.
tags.effect: Visitors of the status page can filter by these tags, and internal emails only go to users with a matching tag. Users who have tags of their own may only edit incidents that share a tag with them (or carry “global”).
tags.example: Set the tag “EU”: visitors filtering by “US” do not see the incident, and an editor who only has “US” cannot change it.

save.effect: Creates the incident or applies the changes. Both take effect on the public status page right away, are recorded in the audit log and notify internal users and subscribers of the affected components. Without title, message and a component nothing is saved.
save.example: Change the title from “API slow” to “API outage in EU-West” and save.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is lost, the incident stays as it was, and no notification is sent.
cancel.example: Clicked “New incident” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without a report.

newStatus.what: The state the new update reports: Investigating, Identified, Monitoring or Resolved. Pre-filled with the current status. Required.
newStatus.effect: With “Add update”, the incident takes over this status. “Resolved” closes it and records the end time; an open status reopens it and clears the end.
newStatus.example: The cause has been found: switch from “Investigating” to “Identified”.

updateMessage.what: The text of the new update for visitors, with simple formatting. Required.
updateMessage.effect: Shown publicly in the history as the newest entry (“Latest update”) and included in the notification to subscribers and internal users. The incident’s initial report stays unchanged.
updateMessage.example: “An expired certificate is the cause; the new one is being deployed.”

addUpdate.what: Posts the update with status and message.
addUpdate.effect: The update appears in the public history right away, the incident takes over the status, the action is recorded in the audit log, and subscribers of the affected components are notified (for “Resolved” with the template “Incident resolved”). A posted update cannot be deleted.
addUpdate.example: After deploying the fix, post “Monitoring” with “No errors for 10 minutes.”

translations.what: Opens an editor at the history entry for the translations of this update message. Only when the page has several languages.
translations.effect: Does not change the original. Visitors only see a translation once it is saved and marked as done; until then, the default language.
translations.example: Add an English version to an update that was posted in German.

translationMessage.what: The update message in the language selected above. Read-only in the default language.
translationMessage.effect: Only applied with “Save translations” and shown publicly once the language is marked as done.
translationMessage.example: For German: “Die Ursache ist gefunden; ein Fix wird eingespielt.”

saveTranslations.what: Saves the translations of this update message in all edited languages.
saveTranslations.effect: Languages marked as done apply on the status page right away; no new notification is sent. The editor closes afterwards.
saveTranslations.example: Add English and French, mark both as done and save.

cancelTranslations.what: Closes the translation editor without saving.
cancelTranslations.effect: Unsaved translations are lost; the ones saved before stay as they were.
cancelTranslations.example: Opened the wrong entry: “Cancel” and choose “Translations” at the right one.

summary.what: A short summary of the incident for the post-mortem.
summary.effect: Shown at the top of the post-mortem. It is only saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”.
summary.example: “On July 1, about 20 % of users could not sign in for 45 minutes.”

rootCause.what: The actual cause of the incident.
rootCause.effect: Shown in the post-mortem under “Root cause”; saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”.
rootCause.example: “The login server’s TLS certificate had expired; automatic renewal was switched off.”

impact.what: Who or what was affected, and how badly.
impact.effect: Shown in the post-mortem under “Impact”; saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”.
impact.example: “New sign-ins failed; existing sessions kept working.”

resolution.effect: Shown in the post-mortem under “Resolution”; saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”.
resolution.example: “Deployed a new certificate and restarted the service.”

detection.what: How and when the incident was noticed.
detection.effect: Shown in the post-mortem under “Detection”; saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”.
detection.example: “Monitoring reported rising login error rates at 09:42.”

actionText.what: What should be done as a follow-up action.
actionText.effect: Listed among the post-mortem’s follow-up actions. An action without text is dropped when saving.
actionText.example: “Monitor the expiry date of all certificates”.

actionOwner.what: Who is responsible for the action (free text). Optional.
actionOwner.effect: Shown next to the action in the post-mortem. Nobody is notified by it.

actionState.what: The state of the action: Planned, In progress or Done.
actionState.effect: Shown as the status next to the action in the post-mortem once saved.
actionState.example: The monitoring is set up: set it to “Done”.

removeAction.what: Removes this follow-up action from the form.
removeAction.effect: It only disappears from the saved post-mortem with “Save as draft” or “Publish”; without saving, it stays there.
removeAction.example: Remove an action that was entered twice and save the draft.

addAction.what: Adds an empty row for another follow-up action (action, owner, state).
addAction.effect: The row is only saved with “Save as draft” or “Publish”; if the action stays empty, it is dropped.
addAction.example: Add “Set up an alert for certificate expiry” for the platform team.

saveDraft.what: Saves the post-mortem with all fields and follow-up actions without publishing it.
saveDraft.effect: A draft is only visible to users who may edit the incident. If the post-mortem is already published, it stays published and the changes are visible right away. Saving is recorded in the audit log.
saveDraft.example: The cause is still unclear: save summary and impact as a draft and complete them later.

publish.what: Saves the post-mortem and publishes it.
publish.effect: Afterwards everyone who may view the incident sees it, even without edit permission; the publication date is recorded the first time. It cannot be turned back into a draft. The action is recorded in the audit log; nobody is notified.
publish.example: After the team’s review meeting, check all fields and publish.

newComponent.what: Opens an empty form for a new component on the currently selected status page.
newComponent.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. The new component starts as “Operational”, appears on the public status page right away and can be selected for incidents, maintenance windows and in the subscribe wizard.
newComponent.example: Add a new service “Status API” so you can mark it as affected during the next outage.

newGroup.what: Opens an empty form for a new group on the currently selected status page.
newGroup.effect: A group bundles components and has no status of its own: it always shows the worst status of its members. A group can only be deleted when it is empty.
newGroup.example: Create a group “Core services” and then place the web app and the API in it.

name.what: The display name of the service or system. Required.
name.effect: The name is shown on the public status page, in the subscribe wizard, in the component selection for incidents and maintenance, and in notifications. Changes apply everywhere immediately.

tags.what: Assigns tags to the component, such as countries or regions. Multiple choice; with nothing selected it has no tag.
tags.effect: Visitors of the public status page can filter by these tags. Tags also limit administration: users who have tags assigned may only edit and delete components that share a tag with them or carry the “global” tag. Components without tags can be managed by anyone with write access to this page.
tags.example: Set the tag “DE”: visitors filtering by “DE” see the component, and an editor who only has “US” assigned can no longer change it.

description.what: Optional short text describing what the component covers.
description.effect: Shown below the name on the public status page; the search there also matches words from the description.

status.what: The operating state you set yourself: Operational, Degraded Performance, Partial Outage or Major Outage.
status.effect: Applies to the public status page once you save. If an open incident is assigned to this component, the page shows at least “Degraded Performance”; the worse value wins. Subscribers are not notified by a status change alone; create an incident for that.
status.example: The database responds slowly: choose “Degraded Performance”. Once it runs normally again, switch back to “Operational”.

save.effect: Creates the component or applies your changes. They take effect on the public status page immediately and are recorded in the audit log. Nothing is saved without a name.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the component stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

quickStatus.what: Changes the status directly in the table without opening the form.
quickStatus.effect: Saved immediately on selection, without confirmation, and shown on the public status page and in the audit log right away. Subscribers are not notified.
quickStatus.example: The payments API is partly down: choose “Partial Outage” in its row.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (opens the component in the form), “Translations” and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: Deleted components disappear from the public status page; this cannot be undone in the interface. Incidents remain but lose their link to it. Both only work if your tags match the component (see “Tags”).
rowActions.example: Delete a retired service “Old customer portal” instead of showing it as an outage forever.

visible.what: Switch “Show on the status page”: decides whether visitors see the component (for a group, including its members).
visible.effect: Switched off, it disappears from the public status page, the availability view, the subscribe wizard and the public overall status. In the admin it stays visible with the “Not public” marker, and status webhooks and status changes keep working. Incidents no longer name it publicly.
visible.example: Hide an internal component “Batch worker” whose status only the team should see in the admin.

slug.what: The identifier of the component (or group): a short, stable key of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 60 characters.
slug.effect: Integrations and the API can address the component with it. It is unique per status page and cannot be changed after creation so existing integrations do not break. Left empty, it is generated from the name (umlauts spelled out, “-2”, “-3” … on duplicates).

group.what: The group the component belongs to in the list and on the status page.
group.effect: Groups bundle components and show the worst status of their children. Saving moves the component; “No group” puts it at the top level.
group.example: Put “Payments API” into the group “Core services”.

search.what: Filters the list by name, description and tag.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved. Results appear together with their groups, even when those are collapsed.
search.example: Type “EU” to see all components with the tag “EU”.

importSource.what: The external source you adopt components from.
importSource.effect: Its current components then appear for selection. Nothing changes until you choose “Adopt”.

importSearch.what: Filters the component list by name or group name.
importSearch.effect: Only affects the view. Components you already selected stay selected even when hidden.
importSearch.example: “Postgres” shows all components with that name or in that group.

importList.what: The external components and groups you want to adopt. Multiple selection.
importList.effect: Each selected component becomes an own component with its name, linked to it. A whole group is created as a group with its current components; the group itself is not linked, its status follows its children. Already linked components cannot be selected.
importList.example: Select “Whole group” Database to create the group and all database components at once.

importSelectAll.what: Selects all currently visible components that are not linked yet.
importSelectAll.effect: Only changes the selection, nothing is created. At most 200 components are allowed per run.
importSelectAll.example: Search for “Compute” first, then select all visible.

importClear.effect: Only changes the selection, nothing is created.
importClear.example: Start over after a wrong multiple selection.

importTarget.what: The own group under which the new components are created.
importTarget.effect: “Top level” creates them without a group. New components are appended to the target group and start as “Operational”.
importTarget.example: Choose group “Cloud” so all new components end up there.

importTags.what: Tags given to all newly created components (and groups). Optional.
importTags.effect: As with every component, the tags control who may edit them.
importTags.example: “EU” for components of a European region.

importSubmit.what: Creates components for the selected items and links them.
importSubmit.effect: Everything happens in one step: on an error nothing is created. Already linked and vanished components are skipped and listed afterwards; a second click does not create anything twice.
importSubmit.example: Select 12 components and click “Adopt” to get 12 linked components.

newSource.what: Opens an empty form for a new external status page.
newSource.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Afterwards the server polls the page at the configured interval and creates its components.
newSource.example: Add your cloud provider's status page to take its incidents into account on your page.

name.what: Display name of the source. Required.
name.effect: The name appears in this list, on mirrored reports, in subscriber notifications and in the outage email.

baseUrl.what: Address of the third-party status page. Required, https only.
baseUrl.effect: The server queries the Summary API v2 at this address. It rejects private, local and internal addresses. A changed address resets the fetch markers.

interval.what: How often the source is polled, in seconds (60 to 86400).
interval.effect: Shorter intervals show incidents sooner but put more load on the third-party page. The value applies from the next fetch.

outageAfter.what: Time in minutes (10 to 1440) without a successful fetch after which the source counts as down.
outageAfter.effect: From then on an admin notice appears, admins receive an email (once, a reminder after 24 hours and an all-clear), and the stale status of the source no longer counts. A single error does not trigger anything.
outageAfter.example: 60: after one hour without success the source counts as down.

active.what: Switches regular polling of the source on or off.
active.effect: Inactive sources are not polled; their links and mirrored reports no longer count. The data is kept.
active.example: Switch off while the provider moves its status page.

save.effect: The input is validated (address, value ranges). The configuration applies immediately; a new source is fetched for the first time at the next tick or with “Fetch now”.
save.example: Fill in the form and click “Save”.

cancel.effect: Input in the form is lost, nothing is saved.
cancel.example: Cancel after a typo in the address and start over.

rowActions.what: Opens the source menu: fetch now, edit or delete.
rowActions.effect: “Fetch now” queries the third-party page immediately and shows the result. “Delete” removes the source with its components, links and mirrored reports.
rowActions.example: After correcting the address choose “Fetch now” to test the connection.

linkComponent.what: The own component whose status should be influenced by the external component. Required.
linkComponent.effect: The effective status of the component is the worst of its own status and that of the linked components. Pure groups cannot be linked, only their components.

linkSource.what: Chooses the source the external component comes from.
linkSource.effect: Only after choosing is the component list of the source loaded and offered in the “External component” field.

linkSearch.what: Filters the component list by name or group name.
linkSearch.effect: Only affects the selection below and changes no data.
linkSearch.example: “Postgres” shows all components with that name or in that group.

linkExternal.what: The external component or whole external group you link. Required.
linkExternal.effect: For a group the worst of its current members counts; new members join automatically, vanished ones do not count.
linkExternal.example: “Whole group: Database” for all database components of a provider.

linkAdd.what: Creates the link between the own component and the external component.
linkAdd.effect: The link applies immediately to the effective status on the status page and to mirrored reports that affect this component. An existing link stays unchanged.
linkAdd.example: Link the component “Database” with the group “Database”.

unlink.what: Removes the link between the own component and the external component.
unlink.effect: The external status no longer colours the component; mirrored reports for this component disappear from the list unless another linked component is affected.
unlink.example: Remove a link set by mistake.

filterKind.what: Shows only incidents or only maintenances.
filterKind.effect: Only changes what this list shows, not the data.
filterKind.example: “Maintenance” to see planned work by providers.

filterState.what: Shows only open or only closed reports.
filterState.effect: Closed reports are shown for the last 30 days only. Only changes the display.

filterSource.what: Shows only reports of one source.
filterSource.effect: Only changes what this list shows.

newTemplate.what: Opens an empty form for a new template on the currently selected status page.
newTemplate.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Afterwards the template can be picked under “Use template” when creating an incident or a maintenance window, depending on its type. It never appears on the public status page.
newTemplate.example: Create a template “DB outage” so the next database incident can be reported in a few clicks.

search.what: Filters the list by template name, title and message.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved. The type filter next to it (All, Incident, Maintenance window) applies as well.
search.example: Type “database” to find all templates about the database.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (opens the template in the form, read-only as “View” without permission to edit) and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: A deleted template disappears from “Use template” right away; this cannot be undone in the interface. Incidents and maintenance windows created from it stay unchanged, because they do not remember their template.
rowActions.example: Delete an outdated template “Data centre move” so nobody picks it by mistake.

name.what: The internal name of the template, only visible in the admin area. Required.
name.effect: The template is listed under this name here and in the “Use template” selection. It never appears on the status page or in notifications.

kind.what: Defines whether the template is meant for incidents or for maintenance windows.
kind.effect: The template only shows up under “Use template” in the matching form, i.e. for incidents or for maintenance windows. For “Maintenance window” there is no default status.

title.what: The suggested title of the incident or maintenance window. Required.
title.effect: “Use template” copies it once into the title field, where it can still be changed before saving. Once saved, the title is public on the status page and in notifications. If the page has more languages, the field applies to the language selected above.

message.what: The suggested message text, with simple formatting (bold, italic, list, quote, code, link) and a preview. Required.
message.effect: “Use template” copies it once into the message field; after that it can be edited freely. Later changes to the template do not affect incidents or maintenance windows already created. If the page has more languages, the field applies to the language selected above.
message.example: “We are investigating connection problems with the database. Next update in 30 minutes.”

defaultStatus.what: The status an incident created from this template starts with. Only for type “Incident”.
defaultStatus.effect: “Use template” presets this status in the incident form; it can still be changed there before saving.
defaultStatus.example: “Identified” for a template about a known, recurring error.

components.what: The components preselected as affected when the template is used. Optional, several allowed.
components.effect: “Use template” replaces the component selection in the form with this selection; it can be adjusted afterwards. Without a selection, no component is selected in the form at first.
components.example: “API” and “Web app” for a template “Data centre outage”.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the template stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

save.effect: Creates the template or applies your changes, including the texts of other languages; this is recorded in the audit log. Nothing is saved without name, title and message. Existing incidents and maintenance windows are not changed.
save.example: Change the title “Database unreachable” to “Database degraded” and save.

newSubscriber.what: Opens an empty form to add a subscriber to the currently selected status page by hand.
newSubscriber.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. An email subscription starts unconfirmed: the address receives a confirmation email and only gets notifications after clicking the link (except your own account address). Google Chat subscriptions are active right away.
newSubscriber.example: Add the mailbox “servicedesk{'@'}example.com” so the service desk is informed about outages.

search.what: Filters the list by email address, webhook URL and creator.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved.
search.example: Type “example.com” to see all subscribers of that domain.

testWebhook.what: Sends a test message to the webhook URL of this Google Chat subscription.
testWebhook.effect: A short test notification appears in the chat space; the subscription is not changed. The result is shown as a message at the top, for example when Google is throttling or the target rejects the URL. The test never waits and is not retried.
testWebhook.example: After adding it, check that the messages really arrive in the chat space “Operations”.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (opens the subscription in the form, read-only as “View” without permission to edit) and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: A deleted subscription stops receiving notifications immediately; this cannot be undone in the interface, the subscriber has to subscribe again. The deletion is recorded in the audit log.
rowActions.example: Delete the address of a former colleague whose mailbox no longer exists.

channel.what: How the subscriber is notified: by email or via a Google Chat webhook.
channel.effect: Depending on the channel, the form asks for the email address or the webhook URL. Changing the channel while editing counts as a new address; an email subscription then has to be confirmed again. Announcements are only sent to email subscriptions.
channel.example: “Google Chat Webhook” for the chat space of the on-call team.

email.what: The email address notifications are sent to. Required for the email channel.
email.effect: A new or changed address receives a confirmation email. Until the link (valid for 24 hours) is clicked, the subscription is “Unconfirmed” and receives nothing. Your own account address is active right away.

webhookUrl.what: The webhook URL of the Google Chat space to notify. Required for the Google Chat channel.
webhookUrl.effect: For every incident and maintenance affecting a subscribed component, a text message is sent there. The URL is checked on save: only https addresses that resolve and do not point to internal addresses. “Send test” in the list tries it out.
webhookUrl.example: “https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces/AAAA…/messages?key=…” from the webhook settings of the chat space.

language.what: The language this subscriber receives emails and chat messages in. Only shown when the page offers several languages.
language.effect: “Page default” follows the default language of the page, even if it changes later. If a chosen language is no longer active later, messages are sent in the default language. Google Chat messages exist only in German or English; other languages get English.
language.example: “English” for a subscriber from the international team.

components.what: The components the subscriber is notified about. Optional, several allowed.
components.effect: A notification is sent as soon as an incident or maintenance affects at least one of the selected components, including mirrored reports from external sources. Without a selection, the subscription covers all components, including ones added later.
components.example: Select only “Payments API” so accounting is not notified about other services.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the subscription stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

save.effect: Creates the subscriber or applies your changes; this is recorded in the audit log. A new or changed email address receives a confirmation email. Nothing is saved without an email address or webhook URL.
save.example: Additionally select the component “Web app” for a subscription and save; its confirmation status is kept.

externalSources.importIntro: Adopts external components together with an own component in one step: for every selected component an own component with the same name is created and linked. A whole group is adopted as a group with its current components.
externalSources.importNothingSelected: Please select at least one component.
externalSources.sourceNeverFetched: This source has no components yet. Fetch it first (Actions › Fetch now).
externalSources.sourceInactive: This source is inactive and has no components yet. Activate it first (Actions › Edit), then fetch it.
externalSources.title: External sources
externalSources.subtitle: Poll third-party status pages, link their components to your own and review mirrored reports.
externalSources.fetchBusy: A fetch for “{name}” is already running. Please check again shortly.
externalSources.confirmDelete: Really delete source “{name}”? Its components, links and mirrored reports are removed as well.
externalSources.empty: No external source yet. Use “New source” to add a status page.
externalSources.urlRequired: Please enter the address of the status page.
externalSources.urlHint: https only. The Summary API v2 is supported.
externalSources.linksIntro: The status of the linked component also colours your own component. Whole external groups can be linked too.
externalSources.warnOverlap: Group and component are both linked (no effect on the status).
externalSources.incidentsIntro: Incidents and maintenances of the sources that affect at least one linked component. The texts come from the third-party page.

adminNotifications.title: Messages
adminNotifications.emptyText: Notes about outages and delivery problems appear here.
adminNotifications.unknownBody: Details are not available in this version.

external_source_outage.title: External source unreachable
external_source_outage.body: The source "{source}" no longer delivers data. Its last status does not count towards your components until it recovers.

webhook_rate_limited.title: Webhook channel is being throttled
webhook_rate_limited.body: The {channel} channel reports too many requests (HTTP 429). Notifications are delivered with a delay. Wait time requested by the remote side: {seconds} s.

webhook_rejected.title: Webhook is being rejected
webhook_rejected.body: The remote side of the {channel} channel permanently rejects notifications for subscriber {subscriber_id}. Please check the subscriber's webhook.

adminFeedback.confirmRemoveUser: Really remove the assignment of {name} to this status page?
